steps_walked.title: Wikipedia lane: the W toggle in the top bar, the first-run wizard, the lane's separate counts, the map layer and the reader's licence notice
prerequisites: The app updated to current main (462145c or later) on your own machine and started from a terminal, so you can put the settings below in front of the start command. Either stop your normal instance or leave it on port 8000 and use the ports below. Each port keeps its own browser memory (language choice, dismissed welcome guide), so a new port starts in English with the welcome guide showing.

THROWAWAY FOLDER A, fresh and ENCRYPTED, used for steps P1 to P5. Start it with `OO_DATA_DIR=$HOME/oo-rowP-fresh OO_AUTOSEED=0 OO_PORT=8010 open-omniscience`, then open http://127.0.0.1:8010. Do NOT set OO_DB_PLAINTEXT: the app then starts at the first-launch screens and asks you to create a passphrase. Use a throwaway passphrase and write it down, because P5 restarts the app and asks for it again. OO_AUTOSEED=0 leaves the source catalogue empty, so going online in P5 mostly reaches Wikimedia. Other ride-along lanes (calendars, for example) may still run, and the consent popup lists them. P5 needs an internet connection.

THROWAWAY FOLDER B, SEEDED and kept OFFLINE, used for steps P6 to P11. The app must NOT be running on this folder while you seed it. From the app folder, run `OO_DATA_DIR=$HOME/oo-rowP-seeded OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 .venv/bin/python scripts/ui_clickthrough_seed.py` (a multi-language corpus with located sources and one Wikipedia article, 'Coastal Infrastructure Act'). Then run `OO_DATA_DIR=$HOME/oo-rowP-seeded OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python docs/audit/living-sources-clickthrough-2026-09-25/seed.py`. It adds a Wikipedia lane with 2 followed pages, 4 changes on them plus 1 on a page nobody follows, one recorded open gap, two extra tracked pages, two law documents and three map downloads. Start it with `OO_DATA_DIR=$HOME/oo-rowP-seeded OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 OO_AUTOSEED=0 OO_PORT=8011 open-omniscience` and open http://127.0.0.1:8011. Do NOT add OO_NO_SCHEDULER=1: it skips the boot-time airplane mode, so the app would start ONLINE and the consent popup in P11 would never appear. It boots in airplane mode (airplane icon filled). NEVER press 'Go online' in folder B: whenever the 'Go online?' popup appears, press 'Stay offline'. Going online would start collection from the seeded sources and the Wikipedia stream. If you do it by mistake, click the airplane icon at once to go back offline. Do P6 to P11 on the SAME DAY you seed, because 'changes today' counts from local midnight. A Claude session can prepare both folders for you.

Your real install is not needed for any step. Know this before you next go online on it: the W toggle is ON by default, so the next 'Go online' there also starts the Wikipedia stream (twelve editions, up to 20 GB of stored text). If you don't want that yet, click W once while still offline. That pauses it and sends nothing. Un-pausing it while offline raises the 'Go online?' popup first.

Take one screenshot per step, and per surface per language in P11. Q1128 = a wants the pass recorded surface by surface. Put them beside the sandbox records (e.g. a new docs/audit/ folder), or hand them to a session to file.
Afterwards, quit both throwaway apps with the power icon at the far right of the top bar, then delete $HOME/oo-rowP-fresh and $HOME/oo-rowP-seeded.

steps.where: Folder A, http://127.0.0.1:8010. First-launch screens (language → the legal documents → 'Create your corpus passphrase' → 'Preparing your corpus…'), then the app opens with the dialog 'Following Wikipedia as it changes' (#wiki-wizard)
steps.do: Pick English. Tick 'I have read and accept these documents.' and press 'Accept and continue'. Type the throwaway passphrase twice and press 'Create'. If the 'Welcome to Open Omniscience' guide also opens, close it with the × at its top right (or Esc). Do NOT click through it to its last page's 'Go online & start collecting', which takes the app online WITHOUT the separate consent popup. If a bubble under the airplane says 'You're offline…', press 'Not now'. When the Wikipedia dialog is in front, read it top to bottom without changing anything, then press 'Not now'.
steps.expect: The Wikipedia dialog opens by itself right after the passphrase is created; this is the first-launch hand-off. Above every control are three blocks you can read without hovering. (1) 'What it contacts.' with a monospace line reading exactly '*.wikipedia.org · stream.wikimedia.org · wikimedia.org · ores.wikimedia.org · dumps.wikimedia.org'; the prose above it describes that list and never gives a smaller number of hosts. (2) 'Robots.': documented public API endpoints; the kill switch, the honest bot User-Agent and the single fetch path still apply. (3) 'Licence.': CC BY-SA 4.0, a link to the page history (its editors are its authors), images not stored. Under 'Editions to follow' are twelve boxes, ALL ticked, each showing the language's own name first and then its code (e.g. '中文 (zh)', 'English (en)', 'Français (fr)', 'العربية (ar)'), and the count reads '12 of 12 editions'. 'Storage budget' shows 20 and 'GB in total'. The share line reads 'About 1.7 GB for each of 12 editions — the total divided by the editions you follow.' A sentence says this is a limit on what is STORED, not on how fast it is fetched, with speed staying with the top-bar collection-speed control. The airplane icon in the top bar stays filled throughout. 'Not now' closes the dialog.

steps.do: Stay offline for the whole step. Before each click, note where the airplane, language, ? and power icons sit. (1) Hover W and read the bubble. (2) Click the airplane icon. steps.expect: (1) Default ON: the W glyph is FILLED in the accent colour, slightly faded, with NO pulsing ring, because nothing streams while airplane mode is on. The bubble reads 'Wikipedia stream: running — Chosen; airplane mode is holding it until you go online.', then 'Pause the Wikipedia stream', then 'This lane contacts stream.wikimedia.org, each edition's Action API, and wikimedia.org for daily pageviews.' (2) The popup lists 'Wikipedia / Wikimedia' under 'Runs on every collection pass:', and its hover names the five Wikimedia hosts plus a 'Transport: …' line. 'Stay offline' closes the popup, and the airplane stays filled. (3) One click turns the glyph OUTLINED in grey with a grey ring (paused) and shows the message 'Pause the Wikipedia stream'. NO popup appears. The bubble reads 'Wikipedia stream: paused — The connection is closed and your place is kept; Resume continues from where it stopped.' then 'Resume the Wikipedia stream'. (4) Shift+click turns the glyph OUTLINED with no ring (stopped) and shows the message 'Stop the Wikipedia stream'. The bubble reads 'Wikipedia stream: stopped — Nothing is connected. Starting again may leave a gap, which this lane records rather than hides.' then 'Start the Wikipedia stream'. Throughout, the fill fades over about a third of a second, the same feel as the gauge needle. W keeps the same size in every state, and the icons to its right never shift. Record your verdict on the animation, and whether anything on screen told you that Shift+click is how to STOP. On main nothing does: the bubble names only Pause, Resume and Start.

steps.where: Folder A: top-bar W and airplane; Home (sidebar) → the at-a-glance strip at the top (#home-stats); Living sources (sidebar, #tab-living) → Wikipedia subtab
steps.do: Click W. The popup opens. Read its lists first: every lane under 'Runs on every collection pass:' will contact its hosts, and Wikipedia joins them as soon as you confirm, even though the popup still lists it as switched off. Press 'Go online'. Wait up to two minutes (or reload). Leave it running 10–15 minutes, visiting Home and Living sources → Wikipedia a few times and reloading each time. Then click W to pause, wait 2 minutes, and click W again to resume. Next, click the airplane icon to go offline and wait a minute. Finally, quit with the power icon, restart folder A with the same command, and unlock it with your passphrase.
steps.expect: ONLINE: the airplane unfills. For a few seconds W may still say 'Chosen, but no stream is running in this session.' W re-reads its state once a minute (record whether that lag bothers you). Within about two minutes W shows a filled glyph with a slow breathing ring, about 2.4 s per pulse; the ring stays still if your system asks for reduced motion. The bubble reads 'Wikipedia stream: running — Every edit in the editions you chose arrives as it happens.' If after two minutes and a reload W still says 'Chosen, but no stream is running in this session.', the stream did not start; record it (field machines saw the lane stop itself after three failed drains). HOME: once the lane has written its file, a separate strip item appears, 'Wikipedia: N pages · M changes today', and M grows between reloads. The item's hover says it is counted separately from your article count. Watch the rest of the strip. Folder A has no press sources, so it starts as 'Your library is empty — head to Collect…'. If that turns into an Articles count, Wikipedia pages are being counted in the press headline; record it as a Q714 finding. LIVING SOURCES → Wikipedia: 'Last change recorded' is seconds or minutes old, 'Changes on pages you do not follow' climbs fast, 'Complete through' shows a UTC time ('Not declared yet' is fine in the first minutes), and 'Open gaps' reads 0. 'Pages followed' rises only as edits arrive on pages the lane follows, mostly each edition's most-read list, which is fetched one edition at a time. It may stay low in 15 minutes. PAUSE: no popup; the glyph turns outlined with a grey ring, and 'Last change recorded' stops moving. RESUME: no popup, because you are already online, and the breathing returns within a minute or two. 'Open gaps' should still be 0, since a short pause resumes from where it stopped; if it reads 1, record it. AIRPLANE: within a minute the ring stops and the bubble returns to 'Chosen; airplane mode is holding it until you go online.' AFTER THE RESTART: the app opens in airplane mode with W filled, faded and still, showing the same 'airplane mode is holding it' bubble. The default-on choice did not take the app online by itself.

verdicts.title: Hover bubbles inside modal dialogs render under the dialog: the consent popup's per-lane host and transport disclosure, and the export row's reason, cannot be seen
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on my own instance (encrypted seed, port 8840, 1440x950). Setup: W stopped, then a click on W opened #net-consent, which is :modal. I hovered 'Wikipedia / Wikimedia'. #oo-tip had class show, opacity 1, and the right text ('*.wikipedia.org · stream.wikimedia.org · … — Transport: direct — protected mode is off, so these hosts see your address.') at rect [539,596,869,705], inside the dialog rect [500,131,940,819]. To hit-test it I set pointer-events to auto for one moment, because #oo-tip is pointer-events:none. The topmost element at the bubble's centre is then a DIV inside dialog#net-consent, not #oo-tip, and nothing shows in the screenshot. While the span is hovered its title attribute is null (show() removed it), so there is no native tooltip either. I got the same result on the Export / Backup dialog's 'Living sources' row, in en and fr: the topmost element is #ux-export. Control case: on a non-modal element (#net-toggle, #rate-toggle) the same bubble IS the topmost element. Every modal in the app has this problem, not only row P's. It breaks invariant #17's layering on the ONE consent popup, where Q1002 puts each lane's hosts and transport. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/P-recheck/P-D1-consent-hover-en.png, P-D1-export-hover-en.png, P-D1-export-hover-fr.png, b_en.json (D6_consent.tip_in_modal, D1_export_en.tip, D1_control_outside_modal).
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:259-266 appends #oo-tip to document.body (position:fixed; z-index:400 at src/static/app.css:1793). <dialog>.showModal() puts the dialog in the browser's top layer, which paints above any z-index in the document, so the bubble sits underneath it. show() at app-boot.js:278-280 also removes the element's title, so no native tooltip appears in its place.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In show(), attach the bubble to the open modal that contains the target before positioning it: `const host = (el.closest && el.closest('dialog[open]')) || document.body; if (tip.parentNode !== host) host.appendChild(tip);`. This works because position:fixed resolves against the viewport, as dialogs here have no transform. Alternative: give #oo-tip popover="manual" and call showPopover()/hidePopover() so it enters the top layer above the modal, overriding the UA popover inset/margin/border. Pin it with a Chromium test that hovers a lane in #net-consent and asserts the bubble is topmost at its centre.

verdicts.title: The W hover bubble (and every top-bar control repainted under the pointer) goes stale after a mouse click and names the previous state and action
verdicts.reason: Reproduced in en. W running + airplane mode. I hovered W, then made a real mouse click on it. The toast read 'Pause the Wikipedia stream', the glyph became outlined and the class wiki-halted. Straight after the click the title attribute held the fresh 'paused' text, but dataset.ooTip still held the 'running' text, and the open bubble still showed 'running … Pause'. When the pointer left, title_attr was overwritten with the stale 'Wikipedia stream: running — Chosen; airplane mode is holding it… / Pause the Wikipedia stream', and hovering again showed that text. The same happens after Shift+click: config is 'stopped' but the bubble says 'running'. It also happens on #rate-toggle: after the click the title correctly said '500 KiB/s target'; once the pointer left it went back to 'Maximum … Click for the considerate 500 KiB/s target'. A reload fixes it. By code reading, the dangerous direction also exists: when already online, a click from halted to running (ensureOnline returns at once, with no modal to force an early hide) would leave the bubble saying 'paused — The connection is closed' while the stream runs. I could not measure that here because it needs egress. The glyph fill and aria-label stay correct, so the primary signal is truthful; the hover is the layer that lies. Evidence: b_en.json (D2_W_en, D2_W_shift_en, D2_gauge, D2_after_reload), P-D2-W-paused-rehover-en-full.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:285-289. hide() runs `cur.setAttribute("title", cur.dataset.ooTip)` unconditionally, so it writes the text captured at show() time (app-boot.js:280) over the fresh title that _paintWikiLane set in the meantime (src/static/app-sources.js:1127-1128), and _paintRateMode does the same for the gauge. The bubble also never re-reads a title that changes while it is open.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In hide(), restore only a title that is still absent: `if (cur && cur.dataset.ooTip != null && !cur.hasAttribute("title")) cur.setAttribute("title", cur.dataset.ooTip);`. show() already prefers the live title, so the next hover shows the fresh text. Optionally, when a repaint sets a title on the element that is currently shown (`cur`), refresh tip.textContent and dataset.ooTip at once, e.g. with a MutationObserver on attributeFilter:['title'] for cur.

OOI18N.t : function(x){ return x; };` then `window.confirm(t("Open an EXTERNAL site on the public web?") + "\\n\\n" + a.href + "\\n\\n" + t("This leaves your local copy and makes a live request from your machine — the site may see your visit. verdicts.title: First-launch data-location step can never be offered: /api/system/data-location answers 503 in the only state ('fresh') where it could be offerable (outside row P)
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on a fresh folder (port 8841, OO_AUTOSEED=0, no OO_DB_*). /api/system/lock-state = 'fresh'. curl and the browser both got GET /api/system/data-location -> 503 {'detail':'the database is locked: unlock it first','locked':true}, and it fired twice during the language -> legal -> accept flow. #view-datadir never became visible and the flow went straight to #view-create. After the corpus was created the endpoint answered 200, but with offerable:false (state unlocked-encrypted). The endpoint returns offerable:true only when the state is 'fresh', and 'fresh' is exactly the state app_is_locked() blocks. So the chooser (ratified as C7, shipped 'browser-unverified per fork-3') is unreachable on every install, not only when OO_DATA_DIR is set. tests/test_data_location.py calls the router function directly with a monkeypatched state, which skips the lock middleware; that is why CI never saw it. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/P-recheck/a.json, P-D4-after-legal-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/api/unlock.py:77-94: ALLOWED_WHILE_LOCKED does not include /api/system/data-location. The lock middleware at src/api/main.py:751-763 therefore answers 503 to it while the state is fresh/locked. src/static/unlock.html:341-347 reads the failed JSON as 'not offerable' and silently skips the step.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add "/api/system/data-location" to ALLOWED_WHILE_LOCKED in src/api/unlock.py. The prefix also covers /data-location/check. Both write paths already refuse with 409 unless the state is fresh, so they stay safe. Add a TestClient test that goes through the real middleware on a fresh store and asserts 200 with offerable:true.

verdicts.title: Stopping the Wikipedia stream is undiscoverable (Shift+click only; nothing on screen says so)
verdicts.reason: On Home, before and after the Shift+click, I scanned every title, aria-label and data-oo-tip attribute and all body text for /shift|⇧/i. It found 0 hits. The W bubble names only Pause, Resume or Start. Shift+click does work: config becomes 'stopped' and the toast says 'Stop the Wikipedia stream'. Putting stop behind a modifier is a deliberate design choice (the markup comment at src/static/index.html:151-154, and the brief S04-09 §6 leaves 'the stop/halt semantics' to the PR and the maintainer). Only the discoverability is a defect. Q702's note asks that users can stop/start/halt/resume, and the only place that documents Shift+click is the operator soak runbook (docs/product/WIKI_LANE_SOAK_RUNBOOK.md:48), not the USER_MANUAL or the UI. The JS comment at app-sources.js:1049-1051 says 'the full stop lives on the hover menu', but no hover menu exists. Evidence: b_en.json (D5_shift_scan_home, D5_shift_scan_after, D2_W_shift_en).
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/index.html:157 wires the stop to event.shiftKey only. _paintWikiLane (src/static/app-sources.js:1116-1125) never mentions it in the title. The comment at app-sources.js:1049-1051 describes a hover menu that was never built.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add one translated line to the W title in _paintWikiLane when the state is running or halted, e.g. t9("Shift+click stops it completely."), with the key added to all 12 locales. Correct the stale 'hover menu' comment. Optionally mention it in the USER_MANUAL.

The code comment says the body exists to tell the operator 'what that decision reaches', and this decision turns the Wikipedia lane on, so the list under-states what the consent reaches. verdicts.title: 'use ORES scores' is pre-ticked on a fresh corpus although ORES is ruled opt-in (Q717)
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on a brand-new corpus created through the real first-launch screens (port 8841): Settings -> Wikipedia shows #wiki-ores checked. It is also checked on the seeded folder. The checkbox is never loaded from any saved setting (the only reader is _ores() at app-map.js:2711), so it is ticked on every page load, and the backend defaults are ores=True too (src/api/wiki.py:254, 274). RULINGS_INDEX Q717 reads '(a) Verify … keep it opt-in', and the gate records 'opt-in unchanged'. The app's own ORES hover (_oresCell, app-map.js:2738) tells the user it is 'Optional, and off unless you asked for it', which is false by default. The egress only happens on a manual Track/Track now click while online, and goes to ores.wikimedia.org, a host already listed in the lane's disclosure. That limits the impact, but it contradicts an explicit ruling and makes a caveat string false. I re-graded it P3 -> P2. Evidence: a.json (D10_ores_checked_fresh), P-D10-ores-fresh-en.png, b_en.json (D10_ores).
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/index.html:1777: `<input type="checkbox" id="wiki-ores" style="width:auto" checked>` hardcodes the default to on. src/api/wiki.py:254 and 274 default `ores: bool = True` for callers that omit the parameter.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Remove the `checked` attribute at index.html:1777, and change the default of the two endpoints to `ores: bool = False` so a caller that omits the parameter is also opt-in. Optionally persist the choice as a setting.
